scope.supports: For Gaussian-integer sector amplitudes a, b, both nonzero, the phase-blind weights (|a|^2, |b|^2) do not determine the unnormalized Hadamard readout (|a+b|^2, |a-b|^2) (kernel-checked for every such pair, not only for the (1,1)/(1,-1) witnesses); mixing always doubles the total weight; the readout difference is 4 Re(a conj b); a zero first sector (a = 0, by w_eq_zero the fiber of weight 0 is the single point 0) or a zero second sector forces the readout to depend on the other weight only, so it descends (descends_when_zero_sector, descends_when_second_zero). Exact fiber and readout tables for ten weight pairs, including the unrealizable weight 3 (for which descends=true is vacuous: both fibers empty).
scope.does_not_support: Complex-Hilbert amplitudes beyond Z[i]; normalized or projective states; more than two sectors; mixes other than the unnormalized 2x2 Hadamard; the embedding of Z[i] into C (non-descent on the Gaussian-lattice fibers gives non-descent on the full complex phase fibers only after that embedding is formalised); the identification of the module readout with the source declarations phaseBlind/mix/readout over Vec GaussInt Bool (H008/H010), which is a modelling identification, not a checked one; any measurement, branch or physical interpretation of the phase fiber.
scope.narrowest_claim: Over Z[i] with the unnormalized two-sector Hadamard readout: both sector amplitudes nonzero implies the weight pair does not determine the readout; a zero first or zero second sector implies it does.
scope.next_test: Decide non-descent of the normalized projective readout w(a+b)/(2(w(a)+w(b))) for n>=3 complex sectors under a unitary mix other than the 2x2 Hadamard, by exhibiting a fiber pair with different readouts or a descending fiber.
